name: Blood-Enchanted Eyes
graphic: Three crimson spiral eyes enclosed by violet branches, ornate gold framing and hourglass details. The palette and eye arrangement come from the live bloodline icon.
history: A goddess born from grief becomes fascinated by mortality and settles at the boundary between life and the afterlife. Her descendants inherit sight that remains open at the edge of death. They can borrow moments and taste eternity, but must surrender something in return.
interpretation: The gold hourglasses visualize the lore’s borrowed moments. The elaborate frame and title were newly designed for merchandise; they are not an official in-game seal.

name: Blue Blade Eyes
graphic: Sapphire eyes, a katana, blue energy crescents and shattered stone in an ornate martial emblem. The official icon supplies the paired blue eyes and blade identity. The revised title sits on a separate dark banner: BLUE BLADE EYES, with SEICHI • S RANK below. The blade ends above the title, and glow effects stay clear of the lettering.
history: Descended from mystic sorcerers, these wielders channel blue chakra through their eyes and weapons, extending their blades with visible energy. Their lore tells of Musa splitting a granite boulder before reducing it to fragments with a sapphire crescent blade.
interpretation: The katana, energy arcs and granite fragments turn the written demonstration into a print composition. The ornamental border is new artwork, not a game badge.

name: Cosmic Ascendant
graphic: A luminous violet shinobi surrounded by orbital rings, stars, planets and ornate celestial framing. The glowing figure and purple cosmic palette follow the actual game icon.
history: Ancient mortal sages meditate beneath the stars. A celestial being rewards their devotion by imbuing their lineage with cosmic energy. Their descendants draw upon constellations, gravity and the mysteries of time and space.
interpretation: The orbital rings and celestial architecture organize the original cosmic imagery into a tall back-print crest. Decorative planets and framing are new merch details.

name: Ethereal Monarch
graphic: Turquoise celestial eyes, descending crystalline tears, luminous geometric rings and delicate silver-gold filigree. The tearful eyes and geometry are rooted in the live icon.
history: The bloodline’s origin story, Eyes of the Heavenly Founder, begins with a god mourning his beloved wife. His celestial tears crystallize into eyes, granting his descendants extraordinary chakra sight and control. Ethereal Monarch carries that inheritance into Seichi.
interpretation: Crystalline tear ornaments and a symmetrical celestial frame emphasize the divine-grief story. They are illustrative choices, not proof of a separate official royal title or item.

name: Eyes of the Forsaken King
graphic: A large golden eye beneath three smaller luminous eyes, with a fractured crown, sun rays and royal framing. The eye hierarchy and gold palette derive from the production icon.
history: Before shinobi walked the land, a family said to have mingled with beings from the stars could bend light. A young king was betrayed by relatives who coveted his chakra. In his final moments, he sealed his powers into his own eyes. Their bearers inherit control over light, revered and feared in equal measure.
interpretation: The broken crown makes the betrayal visible; radiant gold rays represent light manipulation. The crown and frame are new merchandise embellishments rather than an official game item.

name: Shiroi Youso
graphic: A flowing elemental crest with orange fire, blue water, wind curls and earthen details, enriched with mythical creature silhouettes. The intertwined elemental palette comes from the actual bloodline icon.
history: Seichi’s archives describe a clan considered descendants of gods, able to create and control elements and shape the natural world. Their power makes them revered, but also hunted by those who wish to harness it. Vigilance and conflict follow the lineage wherever it goes.
interpretation: The creature-like shapes and central ornamental seal are new ways to organize the elemental artwork. They are decorative symbols of power, not a claim that the bloodline canonically summons a dragon or phoenix.

name: Tsukimori Moonforest
graphic: Tsukimori’s village emblem sits inside a moon-and-forest composition, with a red moon and architectural framing.
history: One of Seichi’s five core villages, Tsukimori is a home, a community and an identity carried by its members. This piece takes its official village emblem beyond the screen.
interpretation: Moonforest is the collection’s descriptive title. The red moon, forest architecture and ornamental frame are merchandise art direction; they should not be read as a documented historical event or official village subtitle.

name: Akikaze Storm Canyon
graphic: Akikaze’s insignia is surrounded by canyon contours, wind ribbons and a dramatic storm composition.
history: Akikaze is one of Seichi’s five core villages. For its members, the village insignia marks a shared home and the beginning of countless personal stories.
interpretation: Storm Canyon is a new merch title. The canyon and wind treatment interprets the emblem visually; it does not establish a canonical storm, battle, or founding date.

name: Akasumi Spirit Forest
graphic: Akasumi’s leaf insignia is combined with a forest shrine and botanical energy.
history: Akasumi is one of Seichi’s core villages. This village-inspired composition also draws on the forest-spirit atmosphere of Shinseina Ki, whose lore tells of benevolent spirits, human bonds and descendants who manipulate earth and wood.
interpretation: The village emblem is official; the shrine and energy frame are new. The Shinseina Ki inspiration is a thematic crossover, not evidence that Akasumi was founded by those spirits or exclusively owns that bloodline.

name: Hyorin Alpine Nights
graphic: Hyorin’s mountain crest anchors a frozen settlement, crystalline shapes and an alpine night frame.
history: Hyorin is one of Seichi’s five core villages. Its official emblem anchors this design: a familiar symbol for the players who call the village home.
interpretation: Alpine Nights and the decorative crystalline treatment were created for this collection. The frozen scene is a visual interpretation, not a newly asserted event in the game timeline.

name: Shirohana Golden Bloom
graphic: Shirohana’s sun-like insignia is framed by flowering branches, gold ornament and seal details.
history: Shirohana is one of Seichi’s core villages. Its official gold village colour informs this piece, carrying the emblem and village identity into an everyday favourite.
interpretation: Golden Bloom is a merch title. The floral branches and seal ornaments enrich the official insignia; they do not represent a documented royal house, festival or historical artifact.

name: Horizon Academy
graphic: The official cartoon ninja mascot appears with Horizon’s insignia, purple scrolls and training laurels.
history: Horizon is the starting village and academy. Students begin here, with Lemu guiding them through training, travel and village life before the Genin exam. It represents the shared beginning of a ninja’s career.
interpretation: The mascot and village mark are existing sources. The scroll arrangement and laurels are new illustrations; the badge is not an official diploma or faction rank.

name: Ramen Recovery Club
graphic: The actual game ramen bowl becomes the center of a detailed food-and-recovery club badge.
history: A trip to the ramen shop is part of life in Seichi: food restores health and gives a battered ninja a reason to pause. Ramen Recovery Club turns that familiar recovery ritual into a piece for the community.
interpretation: Recovery Club is an invented merch club name. The ornament and supporting illustration are new; membership is not an in-game achievement or an existing official organization.

name: Hospital Regular
graphic: The mascot recuperates with ramen, bandage and hourglass details in a hospital-themed illustration.
history: Hospitalization belongs to Seichi’s defeat-and-recovery loop. For anyone who has visited more often than planned, Hospital Regular is an affectionate, self-deprecating badge of experience.
interpretation: The bandaged mascot and club-style composition are new. Ramen is included as a general recovery symbol; the artwork does not claim eating ramen inside the hospital is a specific mechanic.

name: Syndicate Outlaw Division
graphic: The Syndicate emblem is placed within shadow seals and broken ornamental rings.
history: Syndicate is Seichi’s outlaw faction, distinct from its ordinary village homes. Its outsider identity gives this piece a darker, independent spirit.
interpretation: Outlaw Division is a merch subtitle, not a verified named division in the game. Broken rings and shadow ornament are new visual framing; Syndicate members are not automatically claimed to bear Oblivion Seal.

name: Momo Laughing Spirit
graphic: The existing green Momo laughing character is reinterpreted in a jade-and-gold laughter medallion.
history: Momo appears in the game’s summoning and quest content. The Forbidden Jutsu Trial: Momo challenges players to earn Summoning: Momo. This piece brings the familiar laughing character into the collection.
interpretation: Laughing Spirit is the design title. The comic energy, jade border and medallion are new. The inspected records do not establish a complete biography, species, age, or a literal spirit status.

name: ANBU Night Operations
graphic: The game’s ANBU Agent character becomes a masked-operations badge with smoke, scrolls and a crimson moon.
history: Global ANBU HQ on Wake Island offers covert story missions. Operations such as Rusting Serpent send players to intercept dangerous convoys and protect Seichi. This design draws on that atmosphere of quiet preparation and hidden work.
interpretation: Night Operations is a merch subtitle, not the name of the verified convoy quest. The moon and smoke are new; the source agent is not asserted to be the protagonist of every ANBU story.

name: Core 2 Veteran
graphic: The official mascot is illustrated on nostalgic parchment with veteran-style ornament.
history: Core 2 is an earlier era of The Ninja RPG, fondly remembered in community nostalgia. This piece celebrates the time, friendships and stories that returning players carry with them.
interpretation: Veteran is a playful identity label. The parchment badge is newly created, not an official achievement, age verification, or old unchanged Core 2 logo. No exact era dates are supplied because the saved evidence does not verify them.

name: Buff S Ranks Pls
graphic: The mascot, a training dummy and an illustrated statistics scroll turn Buff S Ranks Pls into a scene.
history: A buff strengthens a game ability, and few balance requests are as familiar as a plea to improve a favourite S-rank. This community-inspired design celebrates the hopeful campaign that never quite ends.
interpretation: The scroll’s illustrated training scene is new. The slogan is community humor, not a statement that current S-rank content is objectively weak or that a buff has been promised. The saved original research does not establish the joke’s first date.

name: Wooden Spoon Harvest
graphic: The mascot and an elaborate wooden-spoon harvest scene turn a recurring absurd joke into an illustrated collection piece.
history: Wooden spoons keep returning to community conversation: requests for a spoon item, spoons growing after rain and a recurring motif especially associated with Xevan. Wooden Spoon Harvest gives that small, wonderfully specific joke a life of its own.
interpretation: Wooden Spoon Harvest is an invented scene based on the joke; it is not a claim that the game has a real spoon-farming mechanic or official harvest event.

name: Feed the Server Hamster
graphic: A ninja hamster powers a scroll-like server machine in a richly illustrated mechanical scene.
history: Feeding, reviving or fixing the server hamster is a recurring community response to outages and sluggish service. Somewhere in the collective imagination, a tiny exhausted animal keeps Seichi running on its wheel.
interpretation: The hamster machine is new fiction for merch. It does not describe real hosting infrastructure, an actual mascot animal, or a technical cause of an outage.

name: Buff Potatoes
graphic: A detailed potato-and-training illustration turns the potato-buff campaign into a comic farming scene.
history: Potato buffs and farming-simulator jokes became a shared community campaign. The game’s Potatoes and Abby’s Potato give the joke a real connection to Seichi’s item collection. This piece celebrates the humble crop’s moment in the spotlight.
interpretation: The illustration is a playful campaign poster, not a live claim about present potato stats. The exact buff campaign is documented in 2025; it is not presented as a multi-year tradition without evidence.

name: Touch Grass Event
graphic: The ninja mascot appears in an outdoor, grass-themed event illustration.
history: The community’s Go Touch Grass Event nickname turns a familiar internet joke into a self-aware game ritual. Step outside, take a breath and come back with a fresh story.
interpretation: Touch Grass Event is a merch interpretation of the nickname, not a verified official scheduled event, reward or game quest. Decorative event-style framing deliberately plays on that contrast.

name: More Duck Content
graphic: An elaborate duck-filled ninja illustration answers the request for More Duck Content.
history: Community affection for ducks grew into repeated requests for more duck content and duck facts. This piece celebrates the players who will always make room for one more duck.
interpretation: The new duck scene is an illustrated response to that community motif. It does not claim ducks are a new playable faction or announce content that the game team has committed to build.
